newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Koebnick says yield curve may flatten.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Koebnick says yield curve may flatten.

text.p: The German yield curve, mirroring nervousness about Europe's planned currency union, may flatten as markets become convinced the government is serious about saving, a Bundesbank official said on Wednesday.

Referring to the shape of the German yield curve, which shows the term structure of interest rates, is currently seen too steep for the Bundesbank's taste. Council member Hans-Juergen Koebnick said "it is not ideal."

"In the short term, it may be advisable to consider whether rates at the long end of the curve could be lower," Koebnick, also president of the state central bank in the Rhineland and Saar regions, told Reuters in an interview on Wednesday.
But he also stressed the Bundesbank could not change the yield curve directly and that the government had far more leverage to affect the shape of the curve.
"Further fiscal consolidation in Germany would help to improve market confidence," which in turn would help reduce expecations that longer-term interest rates would rise, he said.

While some bond market analysts said they expected German capital market rates, currently trading around 6.1 percent, to tick up to around 6.4 percent by the end of the year, Koebnick said he did not expect such a dramatic increase.
"I don't believe that the long end will show such a dramatic change," Koebnick said.
Analysts said expectations of higher German capital market rates were based on presumptions that U.S. interest rates would climb soon.
